title: finding(app-shell): `ObjectView`'s entire props surface is typed `any` — a misspelled prop on a public route-level view raises nothing
body:
Found while covering `packages/app-shell/README.md` for #5174 (batch 11, PR pending). Filed unassigned and NOT fixed there — that card is scoped to the doc-snippet ledger, and this is a shipped type surface.

## What

`ObjectView` is exported from `@object-ui/app-shell`'s public barrel, and its entire props surface is typed `any`:

```
packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx:863
export function ObjectView({ dataSource, objects, onEdit, externalRefreshKey }: any) {

packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx:908
function ObjectViewInner({ dataSource, objects, onEdit, externalRefreshKey }: any) {
```

The destructuring names four real props — `dataSource`, `objects`, `onEdit`, `externalRefreshKey` — so the shape is *known*, it is simply not *declared*. The built artifact carries the `any` straight through:

```
packages/app-shell/dist/views/ObjectView.d.ts:491
export declare function ObjectView({ dataSource, objects, onEdit, externalRefreshKey }: any): import("react").JSX.Element;
```

## Measured

This was measured, not inferred, by a planted-defect probe run against the built `dist` while covering the README. Mutating the documented call from `dataSource` to `dataSourceX`:

```tsx
import { ObjectView } from '@object-ui/app-shell';
import type { DataSource } from '@object-ui/types';

declare const dataSource: DataSource;

<ObjectView dataSourceX={dataSource} /;
```

`check:doc-snippets` stays **green** — `Semantic phase: 443 of 443 block(s) judged, 0 failed`. No diagnostic is raised at all.

The same mutation on its two sibling route-level views **does** red, which is what bounds the problem to `ObjectView` rather than to the gate:

| component | shipped props type | wrong prop name |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `ObjectView` | `any` | **silent** |
| `DashboardView` | `{ dataSource?: any }` | TS2322 `Property 'dataSourceX' does not exist ... Did you mean 'dataSource'?` |
| `PageView` | no parameter | TS2322 `Property 'unexpectedProp' does not exist on type 'IntrinsicAttributes'` |
| `AppShell` | `AppShellProps` | TS2322 `Property 'sidebarr' does not exist ... Did you mean 'sidebar'?` |

`DashboardView` is the sharp comparison: its props type is *also* `dataSource?: any`, yet because the parameter is an object type rather than bare `any`, JSX excess-property checking still catches a misspelled prop name. The fix here is cheap in exactly that way — the value types can stay `any`; it is the bare `any` on the parameter that erases the prop *names*.

## Why it matters

Two costs, one of them now on the record in this repo:

1. **Consumers get no checking.** `objects`, `onEdit` and `externalRefreshKey` are undeclared, so a typo in any of them on a route-level component compiles clean and fails at runtime, or silently does nothing.
2. **Documentation coverage over it is coverage on paper.** #5174's whole point is that a covered block should be able to fail. `packages/app-shell/README.md`'s `ObjectView` block is now covered by `check:doc-snippets`, and the probe above shows it checks only that the export exists and the JSX is well-formed. That limit is published in the batch-11 report rather than left unknown, but the limit is this signature's, not the gate's.

Same family as the `DashboardRendererProps.dataSource` reasoning recorded in `packages/plugin-dashboard/dist/DashboardRenderer.d.ts` — that one was declared as `dataSource?: any` deliberately, on the ground that declaring it "changes what is DECLARED without changing what any call site is held to". The same move is available here and buys prop-name checking on its own.

## Reachability, honestly

Nothing a user hits at runtime by itself — this is a type-surface gap, and `ObjectView` works. Its cost is the defects it does not catch at the boundary a route-level public component is exactly where a host integrates.

Suggested remedy: declare an `ObjectViewProps` interface with the four known props (values may stay `any`), and type both `ObjectView` and `ObjectViewInner` with it. That is a one-file change plus a consumer sweep for call sites currently passing props that were never real.

Dedupe: 400 issues read over the window #7083 to #7482 (170 open, 230 closed — closed included deliberately), title and body grepped for `ObjectView`, `externalRefreshKey` and any-typed-props phrasings; zero prior art. Control for the empty result: #7460, #7302 and #7426 all fall inside that window.
